General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1305 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings.
  • As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically.
  • Sources indicate that researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a new study published in Nature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings. However, new research suggests that this assumption may not hold when plastic breaks down into extremely small particles.

As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically. Scientists have now discovered that these newly exposed surfaces can interact with water in unexpected ways, producing reactive molecules that may harm living cells.

Sources indicate that researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a new study published in Nature. Their findings challenge the longstanding idea that microplastics are simply passive fragments of material.

"As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously. Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals (reactive oxygen species, ROS) that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure," noted Wei Min, a Columbia professor of Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering.

Why Microplastics Could Be Dangerous Inside the Human Body.

It has been revealed that the discovery raises key questions about what happens when microplastics enter the human body. Blood and cells contain large amounts of water, creating conditions in which these tiny particles could continue participating in chemical reactions.

Industry observers note that rather than remaining inactive after exposure, microplastics may generate reactive oxygen species, often called ROS. These highly reactive molecules can damage biological structures, including components of cells and tissues. The findings offer a possible explanation for some of the harmful effects associated with microplastic exposure, although they do not establish that this process causes specific diseases in humans.

The research builds on earlier work by Min's laboratory that helped reveal just how widespread microscopic plastic contamination has become.

Industry observers note that in a widely reported 2024 study, the Columbia researchers developed a laser-based microscopy technique capable of detecting extremely small plastic particles. Using this technology, they found an average of approximately 240,000 detectable plastic fragments in a single liter of bottled water (mostly nanometer-sized plastic, nanoplastics). That was 10 to 100 times more particles than previous estimates had suggested.

The discovery helped draw greater attention to the presence of microplastics and nanoplastics throughout the food system.

Growing Concerns About Microplastics and Human Health.

Since that earlier research attracted widespread attention, the potential health consequences of microplastic exposure have become an increasingly important public health matter.

Recent findings suggest that in 2026, the federal government launched a $144 million initiative focused on addressing toxic microplastics in the human body. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency also added microplastics to a federal list of contaminants that may be of concern in drinking water, marking their first appearance on the list.

Meanwhile, studies published in major scientific journals, including the Newly introduced England Journal of Medicine, Nature Medicine, and Nature Health, have reported associations between exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics and serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, dementia, and brain tumors.

However, an crucial question has remained unanswered. If plastic is generally considered chemically inert, how might these microscopic fragments contribute to biological damage?

The latest findings identify a previously overlooked chemical pathway that could help researchers understand these potential health risks.

"Our research found that when microplastics interact with water, as they do when they're in bottled water, or when they're absorbed into our bloodstream, they spontaneously generate what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS)," mentioned Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Wei Min's lab who helped lead the research. "ROS are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue.".

How Water Triggers Harmful Chemical Reactions.

One of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is that water plays an active role in the reaction.

Recent findings suggest that many plastics are hydrophobic, meaning their surfaces repel water. When water encounters these surfaces, the molecules and electrically charged particles near the boundary can behave differently than they do in ordinary water.

The researchers found that these interactions can encourage electrons to move between chemical species, allowing highly reactive radicals to form. As plastic fragments become smaller, their greater surface area provides more locations where these reactions can occur.

"Water is a key active player here, rather than just a spectator. It's integral to making these microplastics reactive. Water molecules become chemically active when they come into contact with plastic, which is hydrophobic. Contact between the water and plastic creates an environment that facilitates electron transfer, and the formation of reactive radicals. When plastics fragment into smaller particles, their increasing surface-to-volume ratio creates more of these chemically active areas," Min stated.

To investigate the process, the Columbia researchers performed chemical and biological experiments. Their collaborators in Professor Teresa Head-Gordon's laboratory at UC Berkeley used theoretical calculations and computer simulations to examine the interactions between plastic surfaces and water at the molecular level.

The Berkeley team developed a theoretical explanation showing how hydroxide ions, which are negatively charged particles, can become concentrated in the layers of water immediately surrounding a water-repelling plastic surface. In this environment, the ions can more readily lose electrons and form hydroxyl radicals.

Hydroxyl radicals are particularly reactive chemical species capable of damaging biological molecules. Their formation provides a possible link between the physical breakdown of plastics and the biological effects researchers have observed.

Could the Discovery Lead to Safer Plastics?

Understanding the chemistry involved could eventually help scientists develop plastics that are less likely to generate harmful reactive molecules when exposed to water.

"Our fundamental work that the most hydrophobic microplastics interacting with water can drive chemical reactivity could ultimately lead to upcoming engineering solutions by redesigning the chemistry of these commodity plastics to reduce the toxic outcomes on health and the environment," stated Head-Gordon.

The implications also extend beyond human health. Microplastics can enter rivers, lakes, and other waterways through industrial waste, wastewater, and everyday activities. The newly identified chemical reactions could influence aquatic organisms and ecosystems exposed to these particles.

Recent findings suggest that co-author Beizhan Yan of Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory emphasized that microplastics can originate from numerous sources, including plastic manufacturing facilities and laundromats. Everyday processes, such as heating materials in a microwave or leaving bottled water exposed to sunlight during storage, can also contribute to the formation of tiny plastic particles.

"This work has significant implications for environmental and human health," stated co-author Beizhan Yan of Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. "In certain environments, such as discharges from plastic manufacturers and laundromats, microplastics can form and enter aquatic environments. This work also indicates that radicals can form on hydrophobic plastic surfaces in water, which could affect ecosystems and human health following exposure. In addition, various uses and processes in our daily lives can generate microplastics, including microwave heating, sunlight exposure of bottled water during storage. This foundational work provides a potential pathway for understanding their health impacts.".

It has been revealed that by revealing that microplastics can actively alter the chemistry of surrounding water, the research adds a newly introduced dimension to concerns about plastic pollution. It also establishes a potential mechanism for investigating how these widespread particles interact with living systems, while opening the door to strategies for reducing their environmental and health risks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that when discussing a car’s performance in the snow, it all comes down to tires and clearance. Tires are the only part of your vehicle that makes contact with the road, so the rubber mounted on your car is the number-one determiner of how much grip you’ll have while accelerating, turning, or braking on slippery surfaces such as snow and ice. All-wheel drive may help you get going in the snow, but it doesn’t help you stop.

So, when selecting this list of best vehicles for snow, we included only top-rated models that come standard from the factory with tires rated for severe snow service. These tires are marked with the all-vital three-peak mountain snowflake icon (3PMSF). This icon is found on either all-weather tires or all-terrain tires that have been tested and are capable of at least 110 percent of the traction of a reference all-season tire. Not every all-terrain tire carries this marking.

It’s also key to mention that any car with winter tires would be our preferred method of transportation in snowy conditions. If you don’t want to pony up for one of these SUVs or trucks with their often pricey optional off-road packages that include the 3PMSF tires, consider outfitting a different vehicle with winter tires. Check out our Winter Tire Buying Guide for advice on which tires to choose.

The CX-50 is one of our favorite compact SUVs, and it offers a rugged-looking trim level called the Meridian Edition. This version comes with snow-rated all-terrain tires no matter whether you choose the naturally aspirated 2.5 S Meridian Edition or the more powerful Turbo Meridian Edition.

Tire: General Grabber A/T or Pirelli Scorpion XTM A/T.

According to recent reports, if you’re not willing to go all out for the Raptor version of the F-150 found later on this list, this popular pickup truck also offers a lesser off-road trim level that also comes with snow-rated tires. The F-150 Tremor doesn’t have the upgraded engine or suspension from the Raptor, but it does have style upgrades and other modifications compared with the standard F-150. There are two factory tire choices, either General or Pirelli, but both have the 3PMSF icon.

It has been revealed that many versions of the Ram 1500 pickup offer an Off-Road Group option package that includes Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires in various sizes, all of which have the 3PMSF icon. Ironically enough, the Ram’s most off-road-oriented versions—the Rebel, RHO, and TRX—also have all-terrain tires, but not ones specifically rated for snow.

The GX is closely related to the Toyota Land Cruiser and is the most off-road-ready SUV in the Lexus lineup. To get snow-rated tires from the factory, you have to opt for the Overtrail model, which comes with all-terrain tires and other upgrades meant to improve the GX’s performance in the dirt and other types of off-road terrain. It has an impressive 9.8 inches of ground clearance.

Ford Ranger Raptor, Ford F-150 Raptor, Ford Bronco Raptor.

Tire: BFGoodrich All-Terrain T/A K02 and K03.

The BFGoodrich K0 series of off-road tires is well regarded among off-road enthusiasts. Ford’s Raptor off-road pickups, the Ranger and F-150, come with the latest K03 tires, while the Bronco Raptor SUV comes with K02s. We’re fans of all of these high-performance 4x4s, but the Ranger Raptor is our favorite of the bunch due to its smaller size, lower base price, and subdued styling.

Subaru has offered standard all-wheel drive on nearly all of its models for quite a while now, which has earned it a reputation for all-weather performance. But not every Subaru comes with tires optimized for snow. Only the Wilderness version of the Outback mid-size SUV comes with Yokohama Geolandar All-Terrain tires that carry this rating. (The Forester Wilderness and Crosstrek Wilderness also have these tires, but those models don’t rate as high in our testing.).

Mercedes-Benz G550 with G Professional Package.

It has been revealed that no, you probably don’t need a G-wagen to traipse through a few inches of snow to get to the grocery store. But this highly capable SUV has become a style icon for its distinctive aesthetic, and for good reason. The most capable version of the G-class is the G550 with the G Professional package, which adds all-terrain tires, a roof rack, a bull bar on the front, and other off-road upgrades.

Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail and Rally.

In a recent development, the Mustang Mach-E compact electric SUV is one of the few vehicles you can get from the factory with all-weather tires, in this case the Michelin CrossClimate2. These snow-rated tires come on certain versions of the Mach-E, including the high-performance, 480-hp Rally and the latest-for-2027 Trail (pictured), which also has extra ground clearance.

Tesla quietly sets up a manufacturer at German machine maker EMAG’s HQ

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has registered a fresh German company whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.
  • Recent findings suggest that neither company confirmed a deal.
  • The organization is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has registered a fresh German company whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.

Recent findings suggest that neither company confirmed a deal. But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.

The organization is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE. Germany’s official company register lists it under HRB 315756 at the Munich district court, with €120,000 in share capital and a business address of Austraße 24 in Salach, a small town east of Stuttgart. That’s EMAG’s home base.

It didn’t start out as a Tesla company. The register shows it was first entered on August 26 as “Blitz 26-299 SE,” a shell company. Law firms sell these pre-registered shells so buyers can skip weeks of incorporation paperwork, and Tesla renamed this one earlier this month.

Business Insider Germany, which reported the change based on a notice in the federal gazette, says three people run it: Maximilian Stromberger, Tesla Germany’s 33-year-old head of sales, an American robotics engineer, and the head of HR at Tesla’s Grünheide factory.

The HR chief is the interesting name. You don’t need one to hold a passive stake in a supplier, but you do if you’re about to take on employees.

Neither Tesla nor EMAG answered Business Insider’s repeated requests for comment.

Recent findings suggest that local press near Salach has been on this for over a week. On November 23, the Stuttgarter Nachrichten reported that signs of a Tesla entry were piling up and that EMAG had briefed its workforce at a large staff meeting the week before. Business Insider dates that meeting to November 16.

It has been revealed that today, the same paper went further. It reports that around 220 EMAG employees will move to Tesla, that the two companies have been working together for some time, and that the deal is about humanoid robots. The full story is paywalled, and none of it has been confirmed by either company.

EMAG, with roots going back to 1867, makes turning, grinding, and gear-cutting machines, mostly for car parts like transmissions and drivetrains. The auto slowdown hit it hard. A year ago, EMAG stated it would cut 455 jobs in Germany, roughly 300 of them in Salach, which is about a third of its domestic staff. It lost €42 million on €496 million of revenue in 2024, per Business Insider. It has been talking to potential investors ever since.

It has been revealed that but EMAG has also been chasing a new market. Its website has an entire section on manufacturing humanoid robot actuator parts: flexsplines, wave generators, and planetary gears.

The first two make up a strain wave gear, the compact, high-reduction gearbox used in robot joints. Planetary gears go in the bigger joints that carry more load. EMAG notes its machines hold these parts to ISO 1328 Class 4 gear quality, with runout under 5 micrometers, and can repeat that in high-volume production.

That’s right where Tesla says it’s stuck. On the Q3 earnings call last month, Musk called the hand Optimus’ main hardware problem and flagged custom gears as a reliability worry, as we reported at the time. Tesla is installing a Fremont line designed for a million robots a year, and the Optimus design it showed in 2022 used 28 structural actuators per robot. At that volume, you’re talking about tens of millions of actuators a year, many of them built around precision gears that few suppliers can make consistently.

In a recent development, tesla moving directly into precision tooling highlights a brutal reality for robotics founders: software gets the spotlight, but high-tolerance actuator supply chains dictate your unit economics and scale. Building physical AI means mastering industrial manufacturing long before mass production begins. When navigating high-stakes hardware trade-offs and specialized talent, having early backers who have built hardware companies matters. Grove Ventures works hands-on from pre-seed with deeptech and AI founders, offering real operator experience to help scale complex physical architectures.

Tesla is already building the German side of this. In July, Tesla started recruiting in Reutlingen to develop and manufacture Optimus parts, including sensors, gearboxes, and actuators, plus the equipment to mass-produce them. Reutlingen is the former Manz site that Tesla took over in early 2025, along with about 300 of its employees.

Tesla has done this before. It agreed to buy Grohmann Engineering in Prüm in late 2016, which became Tesla Automation, and that unit absorbed the Manz operations. Tesla is also putting €3 billion into a Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin.

In a recent development, tesla briefly acquired Wiferion in Germany. Tesla did buy the wireless charging startup in 2023, but it sold the business a few months later and kept the engineers.

  • There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a upcoming world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

It has been revealed that speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Sources indicate that then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of latest careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

Sources indicate that the aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Sources indicate that of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In a recent development, in November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing newly introduced free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

Recent findings suggest that while you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free patch, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

A Used Cybertruck Is Selling A Month Faster Than A Ford F-150

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet.
  • The data from the new iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla announced it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027.
  • According to recent reports, the Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet. It’s America’s best-selling midsize truck and has a reputation for holding its value. Or you might pick the super frugal Ford Maverick Hybrid. But the truck that beat them both was the Tesla Cybertruck.

The data from the new iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla announced it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027. The study looked at one- to five-year-old vehicles and ranked models by how long they’d been listed before selling.

According to recent reports, the Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall. The Maverick Hybrid came closest at 43.3 days, followed by the Rivian R1T at 45.2 and the F-150 Lightning at 47.4. The Tacoma came in fifth position.

Recent findings suggest that the gap between the two electric pickups at either end of the list was even more striking. A used Chevrolet Silverado EV took 107.5 days to sell, putting it last among the 24 trucks in the study. That’s a 68-day difference between two American electric pickups. Across the wider used market, EVs averaged about 46 days to find a buyer, around nine fewer than hybrids and 15 fewer than gas vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that how promptly a used Cybertruck sold seems to have changed a lot since May 2024, when some sellers were cutting as much as $30,000 from their asking prices after listing their trucks for close to $200,000. By December of that year, we reported that used Cybertrucks were piling up on dealer lots, with data at the time showing they stayed for 75 days, up from 27 in May.

In a recent development, then owners got a look at what Tesla itself would pay for a used Cybertruck trade-in. One year later, in May 2025, one owner of a $99,990 dual-motor Foundation Series truck got a trade-in estimate of $65,400 after driving it just 6,211 miles.

So even though the Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used pickup in iSeeCars’ fresh study, it didn’t report what buyers paid, so we don’t know whether owners got their asking price or had to lower it to sell.

Tesla will build the last Cybertrucks at the end of summer 2027, and this will reshape their used market. Elon Musk originally announced production would end around the middle of the year, but then extended the run to fill more orders. And if you order a Cybertruck now, the only one you can get is the $110,000 tri-motor Cyberbeast, so anyone who wants a less expensive dual-motor truck has to look for a used example.

It has been revealed that once the last fresh Cybertruck is sold, I’d expect collectors and everyday truck buyers to look at used ones differently. Someone after a clean Foundation Series truck with low miles might pay a little extra for one close to home, especially since it could be months before another comes up for sale nearby.

At the same time, someone who just needs an electric pickup to tow a trailer has more options. If a used dual-motor Cybertruck costs about the same as a Ford F-150 Lightning or a Rivian R1T, I suspect that buyer will care more about mileage, condition, and how much battery warranty is left than when Tesla built its last truck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.

While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.

For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are right now being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.

Some people just enjoy Grand Theft Auto games for their comedy and freedom to sow chaos throughout cities and for people who enjoy that type of experience they should check out the FPS High on Life from the creators of Rick and Morty.

Here, people play as a human as they wind up being teleported to the alien metropolis of Blim City to become an intergalactic bounty hunter with living guns called Gatlians guiding them to take down the G3 Cartel that intends on turning the entire human race into drugs.

High on Life is as ridiculous and hilarious as it sounds, essentially being a perfect translation of Rick and Morty’s signature comedy style to video game form, and it will certainly give players many laughs as they wait for GTA VI to go on sale.

Ever since Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, flying all kinds of aircraft has been an integral part of the GTA experience and for those who enjoy flying more than driving in the franchise, there’s no better game to check out while waiting for GTA VI sales than Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

The latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is the most advanced publicly available flight simulator, allowing players to learn how to fly a wide variety of aircraft in first or third-person such as airships, gliders, hot air balloons, jets, and more.

Not only that, but the game additionally allows players to fly any aircraft across the planet’s most famous natural and urban environments such as Zion National Park, Mount Fuji, London, and Miami which is what GTA VI’s Vice City is directly based on.

Even more so than flying, driving has arguably been the defining factor of the GTA franchise with the series initially starting out as a top-down driving-focused game and if GTA fans wanted to check out the most advanced realistic racing game, then they’d have to play Forza Horizon 6.

Presently an Xbox Series X|S console exclusive, Forza Horizon 6 has players journey to the rural and urban streets of a stylised version of Tokyo as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply drive around Japan’s wondrous landscapes using over 500 cars.

There’s far more to do in Forza Horizon 6 than just driving around Japan as players can customize a massive estate filled with garages and custom tracks or players can customize public roads to use in multiplayer races.

Some people may enjoy the GTA series for the driving, flying, or comedy but oftentimes people like those games for the freedom to cause chaos in any way they desire, with one game that offers a similar style of player freedom being Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster.

An RE Engine remake of 2006’s Dead Rising, Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster follows the photojournalist Frank West as he sneaks his way into a Willamette, Colorado mall to cover a zombie outbreak only to get trapped in the mall and attempt to investigate the outbreak’s origins.

While players can stick to completing the game’s many time limited narrative cases, players can instantly go about slaying zombies and psychopaths in any way they want by using practically anything found in the mall such as jugs of orange juice, CDs, katanas, potted plants, shopping carts, and more.

If people want to experience a game with a similar story and setting to GTA VI, there are actually a few good games to choose from with one of the more underrated options being Hangar 13’s Mafia III.

The first Mafia game to not be developed by series creator Illusion Softworks, Mafia III follows Vietnam War veteran turned crime lord Lincoln Clay in the U.S. gulf coast city of Newly introduced Bordeaux as he sets out to avenge his adoptive father and brother after they were killed by the Marcano crime family.

While Mafia III isn’t set in the present day, it still features a similarly enthralling and emotional story, one that tackles social problems of late 1960s America and features multiple different endings depending on Clay’s actions and choices during his campaign to take down the local mafia.

When it comes to video games centered around crime, most people wouldn’t consider an entry from the war-focused Battlefield series to be one but in 2015, Visceral Games did just that by creating the crime and police centered Battlefield Hardline.

Visceral’s final game ever released, Battlefield Hardline’s campaign follows Miami Police Detective Nick Mendoza attempting to take down drug dealers and suppliers in the Florida based city only to discover corruption in the MPD and wind up being framed for a crime he didn’t commit.

Hardline may not have been the game traditional Battlefield fans wanted at the time of its release but Visceral’s writing and gameplay prowess managed to make it stand as not only one of the most unique Battlefield games but also one of the most intriguing and cinematic.

Ubisoft is famous for creating immersive open-world titles like the numerous entries from the Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry series but it wasn’t until 2014 that the publisher decided to make a more grounded GTA-like experience with Watch Dogs.

Set in Chicago and the same universe as the Assassin’s Creed franchise, Watch Dogs follows hacker Aiden Pearce who, after a heist goes wrong, sets out to find the people responsible for putting a hit on him resulting in the death of his niece Lena.

What ensues is an action-packed yet stealthy gaming experience as Pearce is able to hack particularly every piece of technology in the city from cellphones to trains and construction equipment to aid him in tracking his enemies down in between instances where Pearce has to steal cars or engage in gun fights.

While Mafia III and Watch Dogs are fun GTA-like titles, neither of them compare to the pure chaos and drama that can be unleashed in CD Projekt Red’s ambitious first-person, open-world, action RPG Cyberpunk 2077.

The latest brand-upcoming game developed by the makers of The Witcher game series, Cyberpunk 2077 has players embody the cyborg mercenary V in the futuristic and crime-filled metropolis of Night City as they get caught up in a movement to take down the corrupt Arasaka Corporation.

Cyberpunk 2077’s reputation may have been marred by a buggy 2020 launch but it has since gone on to become one of the best modern RPGs thanks to beneficial updates and its Phantom Liberty DLC making the game’s core combat, dialogue, and side activities all the more fun.

GTA VI is set in the present day but its greatest gaming influence on a technical and narrative level is undoubtedly Rockstar Games’ previous modern gaming significant hit, Red Dead Redemption 2.

Set roughly 12 years before Red Dead Redemption 1 at the turn of the 20th century, Red Dead Redemption 2 primarily follows Van der Linde gang member Arthur Morgan as he and the rest of the gang struggle to survive against rival gangs, nature itself, and the ever-dominating presence of industrialized civilization.

Before GTA VI, Red Dead Redemption 2 was Rockstar’s most cinematic and immersive game ever made as not only did it feature a far more serious and emotional story than any GTA game before but it allowed players to do all kinds of things in the old west such as hunting wildlife, taking care of horses, crafting materials, and more.

For anybody still waiting on GTA VI or consoles with large internal storage capacities to go on sale, the number one game they have to play in the meantime is the multi console generational juggernaut itself, GTA V.

GTA VI is making records now but GTA V was a phenomenon all on its own for over a decade as it constantly outsold almost every other game on the market for years on end partly due to its campaign following Franklin, Michael, and Trevor in Los Santos but mainly due to its ever evolving GTA Online.

With GTA VI’s iteration of GTA Online likely months away from launch, it’ll be good to finish up whatever players haven’t done yet in GTA Online, such as its many heists and mode customization options, before everyone migrates over to GTA VI’s multiplayer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No.
  • Industry observers note that although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA has successfully completed another powerful rocket engine test as the agency prepares for future Artemis missions that will return astronauts to the Moon and lay the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.

On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No. 10001 at the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center, located near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. The developmental engine ran for its full scheduled duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

Industry observers note that although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data. Engineers will use the results to improve the power, efficiency, and reliability of RS-25 engines designed for upcoming Artemis missions.

Powerful RS-25 Engines Will Help Send Astronauts Back to the Moon.

NASA is preparing for Artemis IV, a mission scheduled for 2028 that aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface. The mission will launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the massive Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to carry astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft.

It has been revealed that artemis IV represents an crucial step toward NASA's larger ambitions. The agency plans to explore the Moon's South Pole, establish a sustained human presence on the lunar surface, and develop the experience and technologies needed for the first crewed journey to Mars.

It has been revealed that the RS-25 engines play a crucial role in making these missions possible. Each SLS rocket uses four of the engines, which together generate up to 2 million pounds of thrust to help propel the spacecraft off the launchpad and into space.

Before any RS-25 engine is cleared for flight, it must undergo testing at NASA's Stennis Space Center to verify that it can perform reliably under the extreme conditions of a rocket launch.

These tests are carried out by specialists from NASA, L3Harris Technologies, and Nova Space Solutions, working together to ensure the engines are ready to power future journeys beyond Earth.

Sources indicate that arknights: Endfield developer Gryphline has a good reason to celebrate, as the upcoming free-to-play action RPG has achieved yet another milestone. The developer confirmed today that Endfield already has over 35 million pre-registrations.

This a major moment for the game, which is poised to be one of 2026’s biggest releases on mobile.

In December, when Gryphline officially revealed the Arknights: Endfield release date, the developer said at the time that the game had surpassed 30 million pre-registrations, meaning over 5 million more have joined in since then.

Arknights: Endfield has pretty much wrapped up closed testing, and we’re in the final stretch ahead of the January 22 launch, when the free-to-play game will go live across PC (where it'll be available via the Epic Games Store, as well as Gryphline's own launcher), PS5, and mobile platforms (iOS, Android).

The developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two new trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also indicates off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

If you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. The game also comes with a wide range of modern technologies, including Nvidia DLSS Super Resolution, and Frame Generation. Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, too.

The Tesla Cybertruck Is America’s Fastest-Selling Used Truck

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that even though it was recently canceled, the Tesla Cybertruck is the number-one-selling used car in America.
  • Sources indicate that in fact, EVs take 25 percent less time to sell than gas vehicles in the used market, and among those EVs there are three Teslas in the top 25, including the Cybertruck, Model 3, and Model Y.
  • “Why do so many electric vehicles, including the recently canceled Cybertruck, sell so rapidly on the used market?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that even though it was recently canceled, the Tesla Cybertruck is the number-one-selling used car in America. That’s based on analysis of over 1.1 million used-vehicle sales from October 2026 by iSeeCars.com. It includes the fastest-selling trucks and the 25 fastest- and slowest-selling vehicles overall.

Sources indicate that in fact, EVs take 25 percent less time to sell than gas vehicles in the used market, and among those EVs there are three Teslas in the top 25, including the Cybertruck, Model 3, and Model Y. And 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used vehicles are EVs.

“Why do so many electric vehicles, including the recently canceled Cybertruck, sell so rapidly on the used market? The combination of sustained high fuel prices and a dramatic drop in market value essentially ‘flips the script’ on EVs when they transition from upcoming to used status,” noted iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer.

Here are some numbers: EVs average 45.6 days on the market compared with 54.5 days for hybrids and 61.0 days for gasoline vehicles, according to iSeeCars. Those 45.6 days are 15.4 days less than gasoline vehicles and 8.9 days less than hybrids. The overall industry average is 59.5 days. Used EVs spend 25.2 percent less time on the market than gasoline vehicles, while hybrids spend 10.7 percent less time on the market than gasoline models.

See all results for new 2026 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 92105.

Industry observers note that and despite the fact that many electric pickup trucks have recently been axed, EV pickups in general are particularly well represented among the fastest-selling used trucks, the study says. Four of the top 10 trucks are electric, and three of them rank among the top four fastest-selling pickups.

Recent findings suggest that the Tesla Cybertruck leads the rankings at 39.1 days on the market, selling in 26.4 fewer days than the average used pickup. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second at 43.3 days, followed by the fully electric Rivian R1T at 45.2 days and the Ford F-150 Lightning at 47.4 days.

It has been revealed that gasoline-powered trucks account for five of the top 10 positions, led by the Toyota Tacoma in fifth place at 50.1 days. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second, outperforming all electric trucks except the Cybertruck.

It has been revealed that however, not every electric pickup sells rapidly. The Chevrolet Silverado EV ranks last among all 24 trucks, averaging 107.5 days on the market. That’s 68.4 days longer than the Cybertruck and 42.0 days longer than the average truck.

EVs also perform strongly in the broader used market, per iSeeCars, where they claim 16 of the 25 fastest-selling model rankings.

The Audi A4 Allroad is the fastest-selling used vehicle overall, averaging just over a month on the market, or 33.7 days, followed by the Lexus RX 450h+ plug-in hybrid at 35.0 days and Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron at 36.3 days.

See all results for new 2026 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 92105.

It has been revealed that electric vehicles occupy six of the top 10 positions, including the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron, Audi Q6 e-tron, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Lexus RZ 300e, Kia EV9, and BMW i5. All six average fewer than 39 days on the market, compared with the overall used vehicle average of 59.5 days.

The Tesla Cybertruck ranks 16th among all used vehicles, averaging 39.1 days, while the Tesla Model 3 ranks 18th at 39.5 days and Tesla Model Y ranks 24th at 39.8 days. Electric models from Kia, Rivian, Subaru, Toyota, and Volkswagen also appear in the top 25.

What are the slowest sellers on the used car market? The Cadillac Escalade IQ is the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average. The Ford Escape plug-in hybrid ranks second at 127.3 days, followed by the Lincoln Corsair hybrid at 114.0 days.

The Silverado EV ranks fourth at 107.5 days, making it both the slowest-selling electric pickup and one of the slowest-selling used vehicles overall.

Two additional electric vehicles appear among the slowest-selling models: the electric Dodge Charger, averaging 98.2 days, and the GMC Hummer EV SUV, averaging 84.9 days.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s clearly a major shift from new to used status for electric vehicles, especially when fuel prices have remained elevated for several months,” mentioned Brauer. “Used shoppers are all about value, which normally plays against electric vehicles. But when consumers see their fuel budget jump 20 to 30 percent, the value of not visiting a gas station leads straight to used EVs.”.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a newly introduced brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

It has been revealed that I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his initiative.

In a recent development, as for the upcoming playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Sources indicate that fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

Industry observers note that as you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Sources indicate that beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds latest palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending patch has been officially detailed.
  • Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.
  • Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending patch has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

In a recent development, the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

In a recent development, the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

Recent findings suggest that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

In a recent development, and, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the next EV to plug in at a ski resort might be the one that groomed your trail. ChargePoint has struck a deal with Kässbohrer, the German firm behind PistenBully snow groomers, to bring charging to ski resorts and indoor ski facilities across Europe and North America.

In a recent development, under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers, software, and support with planning, installation, and day-to-day operations. Resorts can use the same provider for the snow groomers and other vehicles they keep at the maintenance depot, as well as for the EV chargers skiers use while they’re out on the slopes.

Kässbohrer’s first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E, uses electric motors to move the machine and spin the tiller that smooths the snow. It has a 196 kWh battery and can handle up to three hours of normal grooming on a charge, according to the manufacturer. It can take up to 22 kW on AC or 150 kW on a DC fast charger. It fast charges from zero to 100% in about an hour.

ChargePoint states Kässbohrer accounts for more than half of the snow groomers sold worldwide each year. Resorts can start working with the companies now. Which resorts will install ChargePoint’s chargers first, and how many will go in, are TBC.

Alzheimer’s breakthrough exposes a hidden flaw in the brain’s cleanup system

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1391 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A gene that helps the brain contain harmful protein buildup may play a crucial role in Alzheimer's disease.
  • In a recent development, the research, led by John Lukens, PhD, focused on a gene called CASS4, which previous studies had repeatedly linked to an increased risk of Alzheimer's.
  • In a recent development, "These findings break new ground in our understanding of how this genetic risk factor contributes to Alzheimer's disease," said Lukens, director of UVA's Harrison Family Translational Research Center in Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A gene that helps the brain contain harmful protein buildup may play a crucial role in Alzheimer's disease. Researchers at UVA Health have discovered that when this gene stops functioning properly, the brain's natural defenses become less effective, allowing toxic plaques to accumulate more rapidly. The findings could point toward upcoming ways to detect, treat, or potentially prevent the disease.

In a recent development, the research, led by John Lukens, PhD, focused on a gene called CASS4, which previous studies had repeatedly linked to an increased risk of Alzheimer's. Until now, however, scientists knew little about what the gene actually does. The team discovered that CASS4 helps regulate microglia, specialized immune cells that act as the brain's cleanup and defense system. When the gene's activity was disrupted, these cells struggled to respond to harmful plaques. They also became much less effective at containing and compacting the toxic material, allowing the plaques to expand and spread more aggressively.

In a recent development, "These findings break new ground in our understanding of how this genetic risk factor contributes to Alzheimer's disease," said Lukens, director of UVA's Harrison Family Translational Research Center in Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases. "Our work further suggests that defective CASS4 activity may serve as an early-onset biomarker to detect Alzheimer's and that therapeutic strategies which boost its function may offer a much-needed approach to treat this devastating brain disease.".

How the Brain's Cleanup System Protects Against Alzheimer's.

It has been revealed that more than 6 million Americans are living with Alzheimer's, a progressive disease that gradually damages memory and thinking abilities. As the condition advances, people can lose the ability to recognize even their closest family members, including their own children. Alzheimer's is the sixth-leading cause of death in the United States, according to the figures cited by the researchers.

Two major changes in the brain are associated with the disease. One is the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques, sticky deposits of protein that collect between nerve cells. The other is the formation of twisted tangles of a protein called tau. Both are hallmarks of Alzheimer's, but growing evidence suggests that the brain's immune system, particularly its microglia, also plays an crucial role in how the disease develops.

Sources indicate that microglia normally help protect the brain by responding to threats and managing harmful material. When amyloid-beta plaques appear, these immune cells can surround them with protective barriers and compress the deposits into smaller, more tightly packed structures. This containment process helps limit the damage the plaques can cause to surrounding brain tissue.

Sources indicate that the UVA researchers found that CASS4 is important for maintaining this protective response. When the gene was disrupted in laboratory mice, microglia became less capable of controlling amyloid-beta plaques. As a result, the plaques accumulated more rapidly, nearby nerve cells called neurons suffered damage, and the animals experienced worsening cognitive function.

A Little-Known Alzheimer's Gene Reveals Its Role.

In a recent development, "Despite CASS4 being an Alzheimer's risk gene, really nothing is known about what this gene does or how it affects the brain during disease. Our lab sought to address this major knowledge gap with this paper," remarked Addie Walsh, UVA physiology graduate student and first author of the paper. "These are notable findings because they give us latest insight into how this understudied AD risk gene functions in the brain and suggest that CASS4 may normally help microglia respond to amyloid pathology.".

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also discovered that losing CASS4 set off a series of changes in the activity of other genes. These widespread effects could have implications beyond Alzheimer's, potentially helping explain biological processes involved in other neurodegenerative diseases, which progressively damage nerve cells.

One of the most significant findings was where CASS4 appears to exert its influence. Scientists had previously suspected that the gene contributed to Alzheimer's primarily through its effects on neurons, the cells responsible for transmitting information throughout the brain. Instead, the fresh research indicates that its main role is in the immune system.

That distinction could be crucial for developing future treatments. Rather than focusing exclusively on neurons or the proteins that accumulate in Alzheimer's, researchers may be able to strengthen the immune cells that help protect the brain from those deposits. The UVA team believes that increasing CASS4 activity or improving microglial function could eventually offer ways to slow or prevent the disease.

A Potential Newly introduced Target for Alzheimer's Treatments.

Sources indicate that "We are now actively exploring potential roles for CASS4 in multiple other neurodegenerative disorders and developing novel strategies to therapeutically target it," said Lukens, of the Department of Neuroscience at the University of Virginia School of Medicine. "Many in the field initially presumed that CASS4 was likely functioning in neurons to influence Alzheimer's. Our findings shift this paradigm by proving that CASS4 predominantly acts through the immune system. This is particularly exciting, as it has only been in recent years that immune-targeting strategies have been considered for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, and this remains an untapped therapeutic avenue with tremendous potential.".

The findings suggest that the brain's immune defenses may offer an crucial opportunity for future Alzheimer's therapies. They also raise the possibility that defective CASS4 activity could eventually serve as an early warning sign of the disease, potentially helping doctors identify people at risk before more serious symptoms develop.

However, these possibilities remain to be tested. The experiments showing increased plaque buildup, neuronal damage, and cognitive decline were conducted in mice. Further research will be needed to determine whether targeting CASS4 can produce similar protective effects in humans.

Industry observers note that the work is part of a broader effort at UVA to translate laboratory discoveries into treatments for serious diseases. Lukens leads the Harrison Family Translational Research Center in Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases, which operates within UVA's newly established Paul and Diane Manning Institute of Biotechnology. The institute was created to accelerate the development of medicines and other therapies for complex medical conditions using advances from UVA's biomedical research programs.

Lukens is also a member of UVA's Center for Brain Immunology and Glia (MASSIVE Center), which studies the roles of immune cells and other supporting cells in brain health and disease.

Walsh, meanwhile, is preparing to continue her research into the brain's immune system in a new position.

"I will be heading to Boston at the end of the year to start my postdoctoral research with the Neurodegeneration Team at the pharmaceutical company Novartis," she mentioned. "I am looking forward to continuing to study microglia in neurodegeneration.".

Alzheimer's Gene Discovery Published in Scientific Journal.

Industry observers note that the research was published in the Journal of Experimental Medicine. The authors are Adeline E. Walsh, Benjamin A. Davis, Joshua D. Samuels, William A. Mills III, Jessica M. Thanos, Alexis M. Johnson, Katelyn A. Moore, Michael A. Puchalski, Eric J. Steacy, Benjamin W. Wendell, Amélie Daugherty-Lopès, Adrian A. Shimpi, Ukpong B. Eyo and Lukens. The researchers reported having no financial interest in the work.

Among the contributors is Davis, a fourth-year biology student at UVA, who says participating in scientific research has helped shape his approach to problem-solving and his looks for a career in medicine.

In a recent development, "I think that undergraduate research develops a kind of critical thinking that is difficult to cultivate inside a classroom," he stated. "My experience with research has taught me to approach questions systematically and never assume there will be a clear answer. As I prepare to apply to medical school, I know these experiences will shape how I approach clinical care and the broader field of science.".

Industry observers note that funding came from the National Institutes of Health's National Institute on Aging through grants R01AG071996, R01AG087406, RF1AG078684 and R01AG086344. Additional support was provided by the Cure Alzheimer's Fund, the Owens Family Foundation, the Harrison Family Foundation, the Rick Sharp Foundation, and the Steven A. Newman AD Award.

#201172. The Most Valuable Hot Wheels Cars Ever

📅 21 Dec 2018 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1350 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Caranddriver ↗ Open Full Page

The Most Valuable Hot Wheels Cars Ever

📅 21 Dec 2018 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1350 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Collecting cars is expensive, time-consuming, and something of a game of patience.
  • To get a sense of where the market is at right now and where it’s going, we caught up with Hot Wheels uber-collector Bruce Pascal.
  • Industry observers note that before diving in on the spendy stuff, Pascal was quick to note that the Hot Wheels collecting hobby is as broad as it is deep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Collecting cars is expensive, time-consuming, and something of a game of patience. Collecting little die-cast cars is mostly just the latter two. However, at the top end of the game, rare and hard-to-find Hot Wheels can command prices that raise eyebrows.

To get a sense of where the market is at right now and where it’s going, we caught up with Hot Wheels uber-collector Bruce Pascal. Pascal has thousands of die-cast cars in his collection, which even extends to the full-size classic hot rod “King T,” which inspired the 1968 Hot Wheels Hot Heap. Together, the collection is worth over a million dollars, and it includes an example of the most valuable Hot Wheels of them all, the one at the bottom of this list.

Industry observers note that before diving in on the spendy stuff, Pascal was quick to note that the Hot Wheels collecting hobby is as broad as it is deep. He notes that while eBay used to be where auction battles raised prices higher, about half of all transactions these days occur on Facebook fan pages, with regular auctions, Deal or No Deal style haggling, and sometimes even other Hot Wheels fans throwing some cash on the table to help someone else lock down a buy of a car that perhaps had sentimental value.

According to recent reports, you can find most of these places by identifying your segment of interest in Hot Wheels, whether that's the “Redline” cars of the 1960s and 1970s, “Blackwall later cars,” or just plain typing in “Hot Wheels” for everything. Pascal notes that the vast majority of transactions are for less than $10, so feel free to wheel and deal as you build up your own toy car collection. They’re a lot easier to find parking for than a full-size one. Meantime, here’s a look at the Hot Wheels that fetch the most money when they change hands.

2026 Red Line Club Ferrari F40 - $120–$150.

Industry observers note that values of the full-size Ferrari F40 have more than doubled over the past few years, making owning one a multimillion-dollar payout. If you’d invested on a smaller scale, you could have doubled your money too. Mattel’s Red Line Club costs under 10 bucks a year and opens up access to highly detailed die-casts for members only. The RLC F40 debuted in August for $50, and examples are now trading for as much as triple that on eBay. It's not nearly the same money as the 1960s cars, but it shows that anyone can get into the Hot Wheels collecting game.

1974 Magenta Rodger Dodger with White Interior – $3000.

First issued in 1974, Rodger Dodgers with a black interior are relatively common; those with the white-colored interior are rare, as pictured here, and are the ones that collectors desire.

1968 Brown Custom Camaro – $3000–$5000.

The Chevrolet Camaro is probably the most Hot Wheels of Hot Wheels, right out of the gate as one of the original 16 castings produced. Brown over a white interior is among the rarest combinations, although values on these haven't really changed much over the past few years.

Rare Hot Wheels Prototype Camaro Worth $100,000.

1972 Pink Superfine Turbine – $3500–$4500.

Designed by Larry Wood, the Superfine Turbine design dates from the early 1970s and has remained fairly stable in price recently. Wood joined Hot Wheels back in 1969 and was with the company for 50 years, collaborating with the likes of Ed “Major Daddy” Roth and George Barris.

According to recent reports, another Hot Wheels flight of fancy and designed by Paul Tam, the Open Fire is a stretched-out AMC Gremlin with six wheels and plenty of motor. This little green goblin is rare, but prices have held steady of late.

1969 Red Baron with White Interior – $4500–$5000.

According to recent reports, with its German helmet theme, the Red Baron incorporates a bit of 1960s biker culture and has been reissued many times. This original one, with the rare white interior, is the collector’s choice.

Industry observers note that datsun’s 240Z got some respect right out of the gate in the early 1970s, but fans had to wait until 1977 for Hot Wheels to get its first imported car model. These have doubled in price since 2019.

1974 Blue Rodger Dodger – $6000.

A hopped-up Mopar with flames, the Rodger Dodger was built in low quantities with blue paint. The rarity drives the price up, as it has also doubled in value over the years.

1971 Spectraflame Purple Bye Focal – $6000.

It has been revealed that bye Focal was Mattel’s term for a range of colors in the 1970s, and this purple was the rarest of them. The twin hood scoops are a nice touch, but this model has an Achilles’ heel where the body will begin to fall apart. That just makes surviving examples more rare.

1969 Cheetah Base with Python Body – $6000.

Sources indicate that this example is a prototype Hot Wheels, one that escaped into the wild even though it wasn’t meant to. The production model was intended to be called the Python, but the original in-house name was the Cheetah. Since only a handful of cars were built with the early base plate on them, that makes this model valuable.

1968 Pink Beatnik Bandit – $6000 (in package, $20,000).

Industry observers note that based on an Ed Roth hot rod, the Beatnik Bandit was another of the first Sweet Sixteen original Hot Wheels. The casting came in nearly 20 colors, but the pink shade is the rarest and thus the most sought after. Prices have remained pretty steady, though an example still in the original packaging fetched five figures recently.

1970 Red Ferrari 312P with White Interior – $7000.

According to recent reports, almost every example of this Ferrari model produced came with a black plastic interior. This casting has the white interior that collectors obsess over finding.

1968 White Custom Camaro – $8000.

According to recent reports, mentioned to be the very first Hot Wheels to make production, the white version of the original run Custom Camaro was supposedly meant to be a blank canvas for designers. Add flames? Chrome-look paint? By mistake, some of these cars were packaged up and sent out, finding their way to the public.

1971 Red Olds 442 with Black Interior – $8000.

Sources indicate that another model unusual for its color combination, the Olds 442 casting almost never came in red over black. It’s rumored that fewer than 15 surviving examples of these cars presently exist.

1976 Porsche 917 Super Chrome – $8000.

Industry observers note that A relative newcomer to the ultra-collectible Hot Wheels segment, this 917 sprang up the charts thanks to its combo of bright paint and association with Porsche. Even Hot Wheels isn’t immune from the air-cooled Porsche boom.

Recent findings suggest that everyone loves a Woody wagon, but Hot Wheels didn't make many of them in 1969. Again, rarity drives the price point.

1969 Ed Shaver Blue AMX – $10,000.

A U.K. import, this AMX was made as part of a sponsorship deal with drag racer Ed Shaver. Hot Wheels made lots of AMX castings, so the critical thing is finding one with the original side decals—and making sure they’re the genuine item.

1969 Brown Custom Charger – $13,000.

The actual valuation on this little brown Mopar is actually something of a question mark. It’s rare though the casting was very popular, as Hot Wheels didn’t make many examples with brown paint. However, none have changed hands recently, so the actual auction price for one could be much higher.

1969 Mad Maverick Base on Mighty Maverick – $15,000.

It has been revealed that considered to be one of the rarest production Redline Hot Wheels, this purple 442 has steadily increased in price recently to break into the top five of the most valuable Hot Wheels. It was made exclusively in Mattel’s Hong Kong facilities for just a single year.

#201169. GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida.
  • One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight.
  • If you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida. Some examples include the Kraken deep underwater, UFOs, and even a Mario and Luigi reference.

One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight. Not only is it a really trippy mission, but it also rewards the player with one of the best weapons in the game.

If you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the secret Satan boss fight in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that to find the secret Satan boss in GTA 6, you must travel to the northern side of Port Gellhorn and visit the house with “Welcome to the Hellhole!” written on it. You can find the exact location of this house in the image of Port Gellhorn below.

When you arrive at this house, the garage will either be open or closed. The Satan boss fight event can only be triggered if the garage is open, so if it happens to be shut when you arrive, then you’ll have to come back another time. This event all comes down to RNG, but there are ways to increase your chances.

First, the garage has a higher chance of being open late at night. For example, it was open for me around 10:00 PM, so I recommend only visiting the Hellhole house around this time.

Keep in mind that the event won’t trigger if you just wait outside the house. Instead, I recommend using the RydeMe app to fast travel to another location and back to the house multiple times until the garage opens. This worked for me after five attempts.

Once the garage finally opens, walk inside to find two men having some drinks. They will ask you if you want a beer, which you should grab from the cooler next to the couch.

For the next couple of minutes, make sure you don’t do anything to piss these guys off. You can talk to them, but don’t choose the “provoke” dialogue option or throw a bottle to mess up the event. Instead, wait patiently until their van arrives.

When the van arrives, the men will ask you to join them for their upcoming ritual. You should agree here and climb into the back of the van, which will then transport you to another location with a bonfire.

Next, get out of the van and make your way to the bonfire to celebrate with the two Satanists, and wait until they tell you to look into the fire. Once the prompt “look into the fire” pops up, hold down the button to do just that.

Looking into the fire will teleport you to hell, where you’ll have to fight a wave of Satan’s demons and Satan himself.

According to recent reports, satan is not very difficult to defeat, but the fight can be a bit confusing. What you want to do here is shoot the exploding enemies that are running toward you, which will turn Satan’s health bar red.

Once the health bar is red, you want to shoot at Satan to drain his health. When the health bar turns back to black, you want to repeat the process and kill the surrounding enemies to turn the bar red again.

Doing this a few times will have Satan going down fairly quickly. Once you kill Satan, you will teleport back to the real world.

According to recent reports, when players respawn back to the real world after fighting Satan in GTA 6, they will be granted a permanent health increase. Additionally, they’ll be able to claim the Hellspawn Cumshot 12 Shotgun next to the large throne.

This shotgun is extremely powerful and is one of the best guns I have found in the game so far, so I recommend equipping it for any upcoming missions you have.
