Cannabis owners develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1605 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug.
  • The findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney.
  • Psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.

The findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.

Psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.

Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood.

To investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.

The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.

Recent findings suggest that in studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis users experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).

The largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis customers experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.

These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.

Why Cannabis Risks May Increase With Age.

Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, said the findings raise important questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.

"We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large remarked. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine.".

Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis customers and teenagers who did not use cannabis.

Sources indicate that however, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis customers face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.

According to recent reports, "There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large said.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also stressed an notable limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.

"But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis.".

Latest Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25.

The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.

In a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis people. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.

However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.

By incorporating a much larger body of research, the newly introduced analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.

Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, noted the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.

Recent findings suggest that "What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens noted.

"There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is important, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone.".

Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter.

Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.

Recent findings suggest that the late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these key milestones.

"People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens mentioned.

Sources indicate that prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.

According to recent reports, "It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he noted. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline.".

Industry observers note that the potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.

Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings.

Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.

"We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large mentioned. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met.".

One concern is the growing popularity of medical cannabis. Prof. Large said its increasing use as a therapeutic product may encourage some people to assume that it carries little risk.

He has also observed an increasing number of patients receiving treatment for psychosis who had previously been prescribed cannabis for medical conditions where evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited.

"It's got this therapeutic halo around it, which blinds people to the risk.".

Another emerging concern involves cannabis edibles, which can contain elevated concentrations of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main compound responsible for the drug's mind altering effects. The availability of products containing higher THC concentrations raises additional questions about possible psychiatric risks.

At the same time, Prof. Large acknowledged that cannabis legalization could create opportunities to reduce harm, even though it would also make cannabis easier to obtain.

Legal regulation could allow governments to establish limits on product potency, improve consumer education, introduce taxation, and require buyers to receive clear information about potential health consequences.

"You could tax it, regulate it, and require people to show they understand the risks before buying," Prof. Large said.

More Research Needed on Long-Term Cannabis Exposure.

The researchers say further studies are necessary to understand the biological processes that might explain why the association between cannabis use and earlier psychosis becomes more pronounced with age.

In particular, they want to investigate whether repeated or prolonged cannabis exposure produces cumulative changes that influence when psychotic symptoms emerge.

They also recommend additional research focusing on older cannabis people, an increasingly important population as medical cannabis becomes more common and products containing high concentrations of THC become more widely available.

In a recent development, another priority is improving how cannabis exposure is measured. The researchers argue that future studies need clearer and more consistent methods for recording cannabis consumption so that findings can be compared more reliably.

In a recent development, ultimately, the latest analysis highlights an vital gap in public understanding of cannabis and mental health. While warnings have traditionally concentrated on teenage use, the findings suggest that potential psychiatric risks deserve attention throughout adulthood, particularly among people who continue using cannabis over many years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4’s segment in the major Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Aims lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a upcoming activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

According to recent reports, reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as newly introduced quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Recent findings suggest that outside of the Go Pass, you'll also find event-themed Field Research that offers various goodies, including Rare Candy, Premium Battle Passes, and Champion-themed rewards. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though Toyota’s Hilux pickup truck is not sold on this side of the Pacific, most people have a pretty good idea about what it represents. Thanks to the antics in Top Gear in which they were drowned, blown up, and even set on fire, the Hilux has a reputation for being rugged to the point of near indestructibility. What you don’t expect is for them to be fast.

Of course, things are completely different in Southeast Asia, especially in Thailand. There, a pickup truck isn’t just a rough-and-tumble tool for work, it’s also a canvas for personal expression. Thai customizers turn their trucks into insane builds that would rival anything you’d find at Daikoku Parking Area in Japan or on the floor in Vegas at SEMA.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10036.

To put an exclamation point on the launch of its new Hilux Travo Z Edition, Toyota turned to its Australian design department. Noted department reacted, to use the proper antipodean expression, by going off like a frog in a sock, building a Hilux that’s so crazy it’s not even really a pickup truck any more.

The Hyper Z prototype features massively wide bodywork that struggles to contain 325/35 series tires on 22-inch wheels, and more aerodynamic elements than a small regional airport. There’s a table-sized front splitter, a diffuser out back, ground effects tucked under the body, and a park bench of a wing out back.

Industry observers note that also out back, an X-shaped wing that occupies the entirety of the pickup truck’s bed. Planning a run to your local DIY center? Whatever you’re picking up better fit in the glovebox.

According to recent reports, the standard Hilux Travo is powered by a 2.4-liter turbo-diesel engine good for 150 horsepower, but despite what looks like a huge Hilux-branded intercooler here, Toyota didn’t put any power numbers on the prototype. It’s more a love letter to Thailand’s custom truck culture, showing what can be done rather than what should be done.

Sources indicate that perhaps of more interest in a practical sense is how Toyota positions its Hilux in this market. Overseas, the truck is offered in both a high-floor and low-floor model, the latter riding low so that it is easier to load and unload for practical working conditions.

Conversely, in the U.S. market, pickups of all sizes have never been taller, which you’ll notice as soon as you need to load them up. Could Toyota successfully market a low-floor Tacoma model, one that’s a little easier to live with for commercial applications?

Either way, the Hyper Z Prototype is a cool way to shine a light on a slice of automotive culture that’s specific to a region. If you thought authentic Thai green curry was hot, just check out how spicy the country likes its pickup trucks.

Latest Update: Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer.
  • In a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody.
  • Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer showed an elevated risk of developing tumors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer. Researchers at Rockefeller University have discovered that these immune molecules help regulate the growth of cells lining the intestine, potentially preventing the uncontrolled cell division that can lead to tumors.

In a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody. The researchers also uncovered how this protection works. IgA attaches to cells along the intestinal lining and helps prevent them from multiplying too rapidly.

Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer showed an elevated risk of developing tumors.

"One intriguing aspect of this work is that it shows how a natural defense in the gut restrains the cell division that can lead to cancer," says senior author Daniel Mucida, who leads Rockefeller's Laboratory of Mucosal Immunology. "Most cancer research focuses on trying to destroy a tumor that already exists, but what if we could intervene before tumors form?".

The findings may help explain why people with IgA deficiency, a condition in which the body produces little or none of this antibody, face a greater risk of colorectal cancer. They also offer fresh insight into how gut bacteria, immune defenses, and intestinal cells work together to influence cancer development, potentially even in people with otherwise healthy immune systems.

Why the Gut Contains So Much of This Antibody.

In a recent development, igA is one of the immune system's most abundant antibodies in the digestive tract, where it provides an notable early defense against potentially harmful microbes. Unlike antibodies that recognize a single specific target, IgA can interact with many different kinds of gut bacteria and even certain healthy cells belonging to the body.

In a recent development, scientists have known for decades that the intestines contain unusually large quantities of IgA. However, the reasons for its abundance, and the full range of functions it performs, have remained incompletely understood.

Mucida's laboratory investigates how the intestine manages two essential but sometimes competing responsibilities. It must defend the body against dangerous microorganisms while allowing nutrients from food to pass into the bloodstream. Earlier research from his team has also helped explain how immune cells in the digestive tract contribute to food intolerances and allergies.

For the newly introduced study, Gregory Donaldson, a former postdoctoral researcher at Rockefeller who is now an assistant professor at UCLA, set out to better understand how IgA interacts with intestinal bacteria and whether those interactions might influence the development of colon cancer.

"We know these antibodies bind bacteria and, by doing so, can shape the microbiome," he says. "And because IgA deficiency, which affects about 1 in 500 people in the U.S., is linked to colorectal cancer, I wondered whether these interactions might be relevant to the disease.".

It has been revealed that the microbiome is the community of microorganisms living in and on the body. In the intestines, these microbes perform crucial functions related to digestion and immune health, but certain bacteria can also contribute to disease under the wrong conditions.

Missing Gut Antibodies More Than Doubled Colon Tumors.

To investigate IgA's protective effects, Donaldson compared mice that could not produce the antibody with mice that had normal IgA levels. Both groups were raised together, allowing the researchers to control for differences in food and exposure to microorganisms.

Industry observers note that the results revealed a striking difference. Animals without IgA developed substantially more colorectal tumors than their counterparts, consistent with the increased colorectal cancer risk observed in humans with IgA deficiency.

Sources indicate that the association was not limited to a single experimental setup. Researchers observed the same pattern using multiple models of colon cancer, strengthening the evidence that IgA plays a meaningful protective role.

"We found this was true for several different kinds of models of colon cancer, so that was a really convincing effect," claims Donaldson.

According to recent reports, the team then tested whether replacing the missing antibody could reverse the effect. When mice lacking IgA received oral doses of the antibody, their increased susceptibility to colon tumors disappeared.

In a recent development, this result suggested that IgA does more than simply accompany other protective processes in the intestine. Its presence appears to directly influence conditions that determine whether tumors develop.

Scientists Discover a Natural Brake on Cancer Cell Growth.

To understand the mechanism behind this protection, the researchers examined epithelial cells, which form the inner lining of the intestine. These cells are particularly crucial because colon cancer begins when cells in this tissue undergo changes that allow them to grow uncontrollably.

The intestinal lining is constantly renewing itself. Older or damaged cells are replaced by new ones, making controlled cell division essential for keeping the digestive tract healthy. However, when the signals that regulate this process become disrupted, excessive growth can create opportunities for cancer to develop.

Recent findings suggest that in mice without IgA, the researchers identified changes in gene activity associated with cell proliferation, the process through which cells divide and increase in number. Crucially, these changes appeared before any tumors became visible, suggesting that the antibody helps regulate an early step in cancer development.

"We assumed there must be some sort of receptor on the epithelial cells that was mediating this," Donaldson claims.

The researchers suspected that IgA was interacting with a specific molecular structure on the surface of intestinal cells, allowing it to influence how those cells behaved.

Gabriella Lima dos Reis, the study's second author and a graduate student working in Gabriel Victora's laboratory, investigated a promising candidate called DMBT1.

DMBT1 is a receptor found on the surface of epithelial cells that can bind to IgA. Previous research had connected it to several types of cancer, but scientists had not established precisely how it functions in the development of colon tumors.

How Gut Bacteria and IgA Control Tumor Formation.

Further experiments revealed that DMBT1 plays two very different roles depending on whether IgA is present.

When intestinal bacteria are present, DMBT1 activates signals that encourage epithelial cells to divide. This response is part of the normal activity of the intestinal lining, which must continually replace cells to maintain its protective barrier.

Recent findings suggest that igA helps keep that growth under control. When the antibody binds to DMBT1, it restrains the receptor's activity, effectively acting as a brake on cell proliferation.

Without IgA, however, DMBT1 signaling can continue without sufficient restraint. Intestinal cells then divide more rapidly than they should, increasing the likelihood that tumors will develop.

Industry observers note that the researchers confirmed that this excessive growth depends on several interacting factors. When gut bacteria were absent, DMBT1 signaling was disabled, or normal amounts of IgA were available, epithelial cell division remained under control.

Together, these findings reveal how a common immune molecule helps maintain the delicate balance between necessary tissue renewal and potentially dangerous overgrowth.

"If IgA is missing, epithelial cells that are performing their normal function -- responding to bacteria by producing latest cells -- can keep dividing unchecked, leading to cancer," Mucida indicates. "We think this homeostatic effect is IgA's main function. This was a big surprise.".

It has been revealed that homeostasis refers to the body's ability to maintain stable, healthy conditions despite constant changes in its environment. In this case, IgA appears to support that balance by preventing normal intestinal cell renewal from becoming excessive.

A Newly introduced Possibility for Preventing Colon Cancer.

By identifying DMBT1's normal role in intestinal cells, the Rockefeller team has uncovered a potential target for future colon cancer prevention strategies.

Instead of waiting until a tumor develops and then attempting to destroy it, researchers may eventually be able to influence the biological signals that make tumors more likely to form.

Recent findings suggest that "Based on the mechanism we discovered, perhaps we could influence epithelial cells to be less likely to develop into a tumor," Mucida claims. "We know, for example, that having polyps increases your chances of getting colon cancer, so we think that there could be an opportunity to target this pathway after polyps are removed. Right now, there are no interventions available at that point.".

Colon polyps are growths that develop along the inner lining of the large intestine. Although many are harmless, some can eventually become cancerous. Removing them during a colonoscopy can reduce cancer risk, but researchers are interested in finding additional ways to prevent future tumors from developing.

The newly identified IgA and DMBT1 pathway could offer one such opportunity, although additional research is needed to determine whether targeting it would be effective and safe in humans.

Could Beneficial Gut Bacteria Help Prevent Cancer?

The discovery also raises another intriguing possibility. Certain intestinal bacteria may actively help protect against cancer by influencing how epithelial cells behave or by encouraging the production of protective antibodies.

While much of the research into the gut microbiome and cancer has focused on harmful bacteria that promote tumor formation or accelerate cancer growth, some microbes may have the opposite effect.

According to recent reports, "What is potentially even more exciting is that there is evidence that individual species of bacteria can have really specific effects on epithelial cells as well," Donaldson notes. "A lot of research has focused on bacteria that induce tumors or can exacerbate their growth, but we have some evidence that there are bacteria that could do the opposite, just as IgA does. To that end, perhaps we could develop a probiotic supplement that induces a protective IgA response. This is all very speculative, but it's one direction that we could look towards in the future.".

According to recent reports, such an approach would aim to use beneficial microorganisms to stimulate the body's existing protective mechanisms rather than directly attacking cancer cells. However, the idea remains speculative, and the mouse experiments do not establish that taking IgA supplements or probiotics can prevent colon cancer in people.

Sources indicate that for now, the findings provide a clearer picture of how the immune system and gut microbiome cooperate to maintain healthy intestinal tissue. They also suggest that some of the body's most important defenses against cancer may operate long before the disease becomes detectable.

Mucida adds, "Overall, there is a lot more to learn about how the dance between bacteria, antibodies, and epithelial cells in the gut works to maintain health.".

Dually Noted: The Reasons Why Some Pickup Trucks and Vans Come with Dual Rear Wheels

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1104 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The term “dual rear wheels,” as applied to full-size pickup trucks and vans, raises as many questions as it answers.
  • According to recent reports, you’ll often see so-equipped vehicles referred to in official specs or on a build sheet as DRW, as opposed to single-rear-wheel (SRW) pickups and vans.
  • Recent findings suggest that DRW vans are usually the longest and tallest, used for both cargo and passenger hauling.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The term “dual rear wheels,” as applied to full-size pickup trucks and vans, raises as many questions as it answers. Namely, one: Don’t all vehicles have two rear wheels? Good work, detective. The dual part, however, refers to the number of rear wheels on each side. Confusing? Sure. But consider yourself a member of an elite club. Send away for your decoder ring now.

According to recent reports, you’ll often see so-equipped vehicles referred to in official specs or on a build sheet as DRW, as opposed to single-rear-wheel (SRW) pickups and vans. Out in the real world, you’re likely to observe dually pickups towing major, heavy trailers, often using a gooseneck or fifth-wheel hitch.

Recent findings suggest that DRW vans are usually the longest and tallest, used for both cargo and passenger hauling. Simply put, DRW vehicles are meant to handle substantial loads.

Recent findings suggest that automakers go the DRW route on configurations of their heavy-duty trucks and vans designed for hauling and/or towing heavy loads. Having those extra tires means more contact patch over which to distribute the weight. It’s the same basic principle that’s used on semi trucks—having 18 or so wheels spread across the semi tractor and its trailer allows the rig to carry literal tons.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10036.

On dually trucks, the wider stance helps increase stability as well. You can think of the two extra wheels like outriggers, keeping the truck better planted in the face of crosswinds or in turns.

The main drawbacks of a dually setup are somewhat obvious. You have to worry about six tires instead of four, which in turn makes tire replacement more expensive. For dually trucks, the extra wheels sit outside the normal pickup-bed envelope, necessitating flared fenders to cover the extra rubber.

Maneuvering a major SRW truck or van is difficult enough. Predictably, the additional width of a DRW vehicle only adds to the challenge. It’s why many dually trucks end up with a blemish or two on at least one rear fender. The fenders of newer dually pickups are made from lighter-weight fiberglass instead of steel, so they’re less likely to bend and more prone to cracking when they meet a stationary object.

Sources indicate that this isn’t the case with most dually full-size vans. So-equipped vans add their additional tires inboard, which eliminates the need for flared rear fenders. The consequence of this arrangement is a slight reduction in outright cargo space due to the wheel wells extending further into the cabin.

According to recent reports, ever wonder why the front wheels of a dually truck or van have a severe outward dish to them? It’s so that all the wheels match and are therefore interchangeable should you need to use the spare. This dished design allows the rear wheels on one side to mate up with each other, which enables the use of two rear tires on both sides of the vehicle.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10036.

It has been revealed that the need for a dually comes down to capability. DRWs may be necessary to comfortably pull a fully laden horse trailer, a giant camper, various types of farm equipment, or the crops they help sow and reap. To get an idea of how much more a dually can handle, an SRW heavy-duty truck may be rated for a little more than 20,000 pounds of trailer weight on a bumper-mounted hitch, while the DRW variant of the same basic truck with a gooseneck hitch can pull almost twice the weight.

Industry observers note that the difference isn’t as great with dual-rear-wheel versus SRW vans, mostly because both use bumper-mounted hitches. A DRW van may be able to tow as much as 50 percent more weight than a comparable SRW version. With some vans, towing capacity actually goes down when you add two rear wheels. Why go the dually route, then? Because that extra rubber is advantageous to rear-end stability—particularly when a van’s loaded up at, or near, its maximum payload capacity.

According to recent reports, dually setups are available on heavy-duty versions of full-size pickups and some large vans. Those looking for a pickup truck with a bed can choose this setup on the Chevrolet Silverado HD, GMC Sierra HD, Ram HD, and Ford F-series Super Duty.

According to recent reports, in the realm of enclosed passenger and cargo vans, only the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter offer available DRW configurations. You’ll also often find DRWs in use on cutaway and chassis-cab versions of these trucks and vans, which are used in the aftermarket to build things such as box trucks, tow trucks, and RVs.

In some international markets, where full-size pickups are much less common, automakers produce DRW versions of their sub-full-size pickups.

Recent findings suggest that as with any towing or hauling exercise, make sure you understand the limits of your specific vehicle before loading it up or hitching a trailer to the back. Consider what you’re likely to tow or haul when shopping for your workhorse, and follow the manufacturer’s guidance on loading so you stay safe and avoid putting too much strain on the vehicle.

Dually is a term used for a pickup truck or van with dual rear wheels (DRW).

A dually pickup truck or van has two wheels and tires on each side of its rear axle for a grand total of four rear wheels and tires.

You do not need a CDL to drive a full-size pickup truck or an enclosed cargo or passenger van with dual rear wheels (DRWs).

Recent findings suggest that pedants will note that even a rear-wheel-drive dually relies on its engine to power four wheels (the four back ones). In a technical sense, however, a rear-drive dually is a two-wheel-drive vehicle, since power is sent to the drive wheels via two axle shafts. Similarly, though a four-wheel-drive-equipped dually may power a total of six wheels, the engine’s power only reaches the drive wheels via a total of four axle shafts (two at each end).

Throughout its social media accounts, Team Cherry has unveiled their Cherry Time! Livestream, a newly introduced presentation they haven’t done before. You can watch it live on November 27, 7 AM PT on their official YouTube channel.

Sources indicate that team Cherry is promising “a bunch of exciting announcements” aside from the already expected info on Sea of Sorrow, the Silksong DLC. This could be either upcoming updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

According to recent reports, aside from the initial trailer released back in 2025, the team has been radio silent about its development. This might actually be a great sign, as you’ll know if you’ve followed anything about Silksong’s development cycle in the past years.

According to recent reports, the game was originally conceived as an expansion for the original Hollow Knight, where you could play as the supporting character Hornet. However, the project became too significant for its own good, eventually turning into a whole fresh game in just a few years.

This could be either new updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

Recent findings suggest that however, Team Cherry was adamant about never feeding us any new info, leading fans to think the game was quietly canceled or that it was all a hoax from the start. You’ll certainly remember those frenzied fans typing “SKONG??!!” on every single indie game announcement stream (or any stream, really). Things got out of control at a time.

According to recent reports, imagine the shock when we discovered Team Cherry was just too busy adding latest things to the game over the years and had adopted a chronically offline posture. We only got actual info less than a month before the game actually came out. We might be seeing history repeating itself here, but I wouldn’t count on it just yet.

While we were promised that the waiting wouldn’t be as daunting as it was for the base game (which took 8 years to release after the first title), it seems like Sea of Sorrow might be going through the same development hell cycle.

The recently released physical edition of Silksong for the Nintendo Switch presented the upcoming DLC as a “giant expansion” and made no newly introduced notes to the 2026 release window, as shown by Reddit user ArchivistOfSkylands.

Sources indicate that for all we know, Team Cherry might be taking their time cooking another huge meal for us once again. It certainly won’t take 8 more years again, but we might not be visiting this newly introduced ocean of content this year just yet.

According to recent reports, the original Hollow Knight had a total of four free updates, which added tons of content such as newly introduced endings, more quests, new bosses, and many boss gauntlets to prove yourself as a real God in Hallownest. Fans have huge expectations for Silksong to get the same treatment, especially when it comes to the latter.

Sources indicate that we’ll know more about the current state of this expansion in just a few more days. We got a release date for Silksong similarly, coming almost out of nowhere, so it might be the time. But as we’ve seen lately, devs have been taking extra time to refine their final game, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see that happen here, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nioh 3 has received a hot latest update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for patch 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an problem that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an problem that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Recent findings suggest that team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an concern that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

According to recent reports, hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

Sources indicate that as is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the tech giant's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be declared tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

Industry observers note that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

In a recent development, what do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

Scientists discover a fresh type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants.
  • Recent findings suggest that the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression.
  • Sources indicate that circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, showed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

Sources indicate that circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied.

To investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

Industry observers note that the researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

Those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

Sources indicate that the differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

It has been revealed that first author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:.

"Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them.".

Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective.

One of the most key implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

Sources indicate that medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

According to recent reports, however, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

Because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

Co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:.

"Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

"For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is crucial to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.".

A New Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People.

Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially notable for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

"We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

"Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition.".

  • Recent findings suggest that the big latest arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest significant content patch has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

Recent findings suggest that the big latest arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Industry observers note that varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

In a recent development, the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Recent findings suggest that staying on the theme of reminiscence, the major event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Sources indicate that outside of events, there’s a newly introduced set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Industry News: Latest gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed.
  • According to recent reports, developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light.
  • Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed. Unlike conventional approaches that can eliminate both good and bad bacteria, the new therapy is designed to target specific microbes responsible for damaging gums and the bone that supports teeth.

According to recent reports, developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light. Early experiments in human cell cultures and mice suggest that it could offer a more precise way to combat periodontitis, a serious form of gum disease that can eventually lead to tooth loss. The findings were published in the Journal of Translational Medicine.

Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.

It has been revealed that the human mouth contains a complex community of microorganisms, many of which play important roles in maintaining oral health. Problems can arise when harmful bacteria multiply and disturb this delicate balance.

In a recent development, one particularly troublesome species is Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which scientists classify as a keystone pathogen. This means it can have an outsized influence on the surrounding microbial community, even when it is not especially abundant. By promoting inflammation and disrupting the normal balance of oral bacteria, it can contribute to the destruction of the bone that holds teeth in place.

Treating periodontitis often involves eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. However, some existing antimicrobial treatments do not distinguish between harmful organisms and microbes that help maintain a healthy mouth.

Recent findings suggest that "Current treatments for periodontitis, including antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), eliminate both pathogenic and beneficial oral bacteria," remarked Kazuhide Sato, one of the corresponding authors and a lecturer at Nagoya University. "These approaches often disrupt the entire oral microbial ecosystem and can also release lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an endotoxin that may exacerbate inflammation.".

Scientists Adapt Cancer Therapy to Target Gum Disease Bacteria.

In a recent development, to overcome these limitations, the Nagoya University team turned to a technology originally designed to treat cancer. Known as near-infrared photoimmunotherapy, it uses antibodies linked to a light-sensitive dye to recognize specific targets. Once the compound attaches to its intended target, exposure to near-infrared light activates the dye and produces a damaging effect.

It has been revealed that the researchers adapted this strategy to attack P. gingivalis without unnecessarily disturbing other oral bacteria. Their approach relies on IgY, a type of antibody collected from the egg yolks of hens that have been immunized against the pathogen.

Egg yolk antibodies offer a practical advantage because they can be produced in large quantities at relatively low cost. This could make them an attractive option for developing targeted treatments that are affordable and scalable.

According to recent reports, the resulting technology, called near-infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT²), was developed by researchers at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine. The team included first author Hiroshi Maruyama, Professor Hideharu Hibi, and corresponding authors Sato and Kiyoshi Sakai.

Industry observers note that to determine whether the treatment could destroy harmful bacteria while protecting healthy tissue, the researchers tested it in human cell cultures and mice. They also compared its effects with those of conventional antimicrobial therapies.

Light-Activated Antibodies Destroy Harmful Bacteria.

Laboratory experiments highlighted that the antibody and dye combination attached specifically to P. gingivalis. Other bacterial species and healthy human gum cells were left unaffected.

When the researchers illuminated the targeted bacteria with near-infrared light, the activated dye damaged their outer membranes, ultimately killing them.

Industry observers note that microscopic examination revealed an notable difference between this technique and conventional antimicrobial light therapy. Bacteria exposed to the latest treatment developed tiny openings in their membranes but largely maintained their overall shape. By contrast, conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy caused the bacteria to break apart completely.

The distinction matters because destroying bacterial cells can release substances that contribute to inflammation. Preserving the overall structure of the targeted bacteria, even after killing them, could help limit this unwanted effect.

The researchers also examined how the treatments affected healthy human gum cells. Their targeted therapy caused no detectable harm to these cells, while conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy produced cellular damage and slowed healing.

Newly introduced Treatment Reduces Bone Loss in Mice.

The team next investigated whether these laboratory findings would translate into meaningful improvements in gum disease.

Sources indicate that in mice with periodontitis, the experimental therapy significantly reduced the loss of alveolar bone, the part of the jawbone that surrounds and supports teeth. Preventing this type of bone deterioration is especially notable because advanced periodontitis can loosen teeth and eventually cause them to fall out.

Analysis of the animals' saliva revealed another encouraging result. The treatment reduced P. gingivalis while preserving beneficial Streptococcus bacteria, helping maintain a healthier balance of microorganisms in the mouth.

Conventional antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, on the other hand, eliminated both harmful and beneficial bacteria in the experiments, causing broader disruption to the oral microbial community.

"Results demonstrated that, unlike antibiotics or standard light therapy, this approach selectively removes the primary pathogenic species while preserving the remainder of the oral bacterial community," Sato said.

Together, the findings suggest that targeting individual disease-causing bacteria could help control gum disease while avoiding some of the unintended consequences of broader antimicrobial treatments.

AI Could Help Develop More Precise Gum Disease Treatments.

Although the early results are promising, the researchers recognize that periodontitis is a complex disease involving multiple bacterial species. Eliminating P. gingivalis alone may not be sufficient to treat every case.

Industry observers note that to address this challenge, the team prepares to use artificial intelligence (AI) to examine publicly available information about oral bacteria. By identifying other important microorganisms and studying how different species interact, they hope to uncover additional targets for future therapies.

Sources indicate that the researchers also see potential implications beyond oral health. Periodontitis has been linked to several other medical conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.

Understanding the relationships between oral bacteria and these conditions could eventually help scientists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific treatments. AI analysis may play a role in making those decisions and guiding the development of more personalized approaches to gum disease.

For now, the therapy remains experimental, with its effectiveness demonstrated in laboratory studies and mice rather than human clinical trials. However, the findings point toward a possible future in which treating gum disease means selectively removing harmful bacteria instead of disrupting the entire microbial community that helps keep the mouth healthy.

Tech Report: Take-Two's GTA 6 PC Port Crackdown Has Already Taken Down Over 3,000 Repositories

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (559 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer.
  • The developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build.
  • It has been revealed that gitHub claims it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer. Unlike some of the fan-made PC ports we've seen for older console games, though, this one was being developed using a build of a game that had only just come out.

The developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build. The organization requested that GitHub take down Leonida and its forks, arguing that the alleged infringement couldn't be addressed without disabling the repositories altogether.

It has been revealed that gitHub claims it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories. That number includes forks, which are essentially copies of a repository that other GitHub consumers can work on independently. That doesn't mean there were 3,007 different GTA 6 PC ports in development, though.

An Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

Industry observers note that according to PC Gamer, the team appeared to have reached the game's splash screen during a livestream before it crashed. The project's lead developer, NotRexed, subsequently announced their departure, citing the loss of the Discord server as well as the pressure of managing the community alongside school and sports.

Take-Two's takedown hasn't put an end to Leonida, either. According to the same report, others have already tried to pick up where the original developer left off.

It's a familiar situation for those of us who primarily play on PC. GTA 4 came to PC several months after its console debut, while we had to wait more than a year and a half after GTA 5's original launch for its PC version. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly a year to make its way over.

Sources indicate that the difference this time is that a report has suggested GTA 6 could arrive on PC in the first quarter of 2027. If that turns out to be true, the wait would be much shorter than it was for Rockstar's last two major releases. There hasn't been an official announcement confirming that release window, however.

Sources indicate that getting GTA 6 to boot on a PC and getting it to run well enough to play through the entire game are two very different things. Just look at how badly Rockstar handled GTA 4's PC port. Even hardware that far exceeded the game's original system requirements struggled to run it smoothly, and Rockstar never bothered to properly fix it.

Modders have spent years ironing out its performance challenges and bugs, and while that's still an ongoing process, I'd argue 2026 has been the best year yet to play GTA 4 on PC. Even if one of these unofficial efforts eventually makes it past the splash screen, there's no telling how well the game will run on a typical gaming PC or whether it'll have major bugs throughout the story.

Hopefully, Rockstar won't keep us in the dark for too long regarding the official PC version. Even an approximate release window would be welcome at this point, especially for anyone holding off on buying a console just to play GTA 6.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has revealed that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

It has been revealed that on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still indicates that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

Tech Report: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes.
  • The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage.
  • Industry observers note that in their upcoming paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.

The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.

Industry observers note that in their upcoming paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.

Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem.

Recent findings suggest that unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.

For years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.

According to recent reports, however, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?

As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.

To overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.

It has been revealed that "Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," remarked Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem.".

Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers.".

70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates.

Sources indicate that one of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.

Quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.

Sources indicate that in one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates.".

Quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.

Recent findings suggest that by encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.

"We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," mentioned Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a new foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically.".

Sources indicate that the researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.

Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.

By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are right now out of reach.

The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.
